::: {#cell-2 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
import time

from sudoku.cell import *
from sudoku.board import *
```
:::


You can create a Board from a list of 9 lines of 9 chars each. Legal chars are the numbers from 1 to 9 and - for empty cell

::: {#cell-4 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# medium
board = ['5-------6', 
         '-816---5-', 
         '--2-5-14-', 
         '----7--3-', 
         '--71-69--',
         '-1--3----', 
         '-26-4-7--', 
         '-5---249-', 
         '8-------2']
b = Board(board)
```
:::


::: {#cell-5 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
def foo():
    board_wrong_format_1 = ['---------', 
         '---------', 
         '----7--3-', 
         '--71-----',
         '-1--3----', 
         '-26-4-7--', 
         '-5-------', 
         '8--------']
    return Board(board_wrong_format_1)

test_fail(foo)
```
:::


::: {#cell-6 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
def foo2():
    board_wrong_format_2 = ['---------', 
         '---------']
    return Board(board_wrong_format_1)

test_fail(foo2)
```
:::


A board can be exported, generating a line of text which can be imported in external sites, like [Sudoku solutions](https://www.sudoku-solutions.com/)

::: {#cell-8 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
b.export()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
```
'5       6 816   5   2 5 14     7  3   71 69   1  3     26 4 7   5   249 8       2'
```
:::
:::


::: {#cell-9 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# hard
board = ['----5163-', 
         '----94---', 
         '--3-6--94', 
         '6-7------', 
         '-386--5--', 
         '9-1------', 
         '--6-1--57', 
         '----26---', 
         '----3786-']
b = Board(board)
```
:::


You can try to solve a board:

::: {#cell-11 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
b.solve()
```

To solve a very hard puzzle, chances are you will need to use brute force

::: {#cell-13 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# very hard 1
board = ['8-----41-', 
         '-6-9-----', 
         '3-2------', 
         '-5---814-', 
         '4----1--3', 
         '-8---326-', 
         '1-9------', 
         '-7-3-----', 
         '2-----85-']
b = Board(board)
```
:::


::: {#cell-14 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# very hard 2
board = ['4-------8', 
         '--9-1--7-', 
         '-23--54--', 
         '-----26--', 
         '-9--5--4-', 
         '--71-----', 
         '--24--39-', 
         '-7--6-5--', 
         '1-------4']
b = Board(board)
```
:::


::: {#cell-15 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
b = Board(board)
res = b.solve()
test_eq(res, Solution.NOT_FOUND)
res.value
```

The solver detects a puzzle with no solutions

::: {#cell-18 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
already_inconsistent_board = ['4--4----8', 
         '--9-1--7-', 
         '-23--54--', 
         '-----26--', 
         '-9--5--4-', 
         '--71-----', 
         '--24--39-', 
         '-7--6-5--', 
         '1-------4']
b = Board(already_inconsistent_board)
res = b.solve()
test_eq(res, Solution.NO_SOLUTIONS)
res.value
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
```
'no solutions'
```
:::
:::


::: {#cell-19 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
board_no_solutions = ['4-52--9-8', 
         '--9-1427-', 
         '723--54--', 
         '-----26--', 
         '29--5-14-', 
         '--71--82-', 
         '--24--39-', 
         '974-6-5-2', 
         '13-5297-4']
b = Board(board_no_solutions)
res = b.solve()
test_eq(res, Solution.NO_SOLUTIONS)
res.value
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
```
'no solutions'
```
:::
:::


Trying to solve a puzzle with more than one solution, the solver picks one of them (you'll need to use brute force)

::: {#cell-21 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
board_many_solutions = ['123456789', 
         '---------', 
         '---------', 
         '---------', 
         '---------', 
         '---------', 
         '---------', 
         '---------', 
         '---------']
b = Board(board_many_solutions)
res = b.solve(True)
test_eq(res, Solution.ONE_SOLUTION)
res.value
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

However, you can check the existence of more than one solution

::: {#cell-23 .cell}
``` {.python .cell-code}
b = Board(board_many_solutions)
res = b.solve(True, print_log=True, check_many_solutions=True)
test_eq(res, Solution.MULTIPLE_SOLUTIONS)
res.value
```
